interpretation: This was an independent repeat of the earlier round-robin serving configuration at N53. It used 4,096-token prefill chunks and dense decode CUDA graph sizes 1–64. Round-robin sends prompts across the two prefill workers; CUDA graphs aim to reduce launch overhead. Runtime logs show FA3 attention and auto MoE/all-reduce settings, rather than the later MNNVL plus FlashInfer decode combination. The minimum recorded TTFT is an observation of this complete setup; this report does not isolate how much each optimisation contributed.

interpretation: This early topology trial allocated more GPUs to decode: three independent TP4/EP4 decode workers, with only two TP2 prefill workers. At N16, relatively few requests compete for those workers. That is a plausible explanation for the low ITL, but it is not an isolated causal test. This run did not use the later explicit DeepGEMM, MNNVL, FlashInfer decode or 4,096-token prefill tuning. Its latency record does not make it the best aggregate-throughput configuration.

This topology allocated 12 GPUs to three TP4 prefill workers and four GPUs to one TP4/EP4 decode worker. N16 is a light load compared with the current goodput frontier. Every evaluated request in the selected full run met both latency limits. This demonstrates a 100% observed pass rate at that load, not a uniquely superior backend or capacity limit.

configuration.loader_policy_effect: Built-in prefetch enables background page-cache warming and implicitly selects single-thread iterator with default extra_config. Two TP4 replicas have independent prefetch rank groups; no guaranteed node-wide deduplication.
configuration.hypothesis: Potential shared-storage page-fault/CPU contention; not isolated from expert-sharding, CPU affinity or cache state.

interpretation: This H100 trial added checkpoint weight prefetch to reduce loading time. Prefetch is a startup and allocation-cost hypothesis, not inherently a faster per-token inference method. The historical short allocation is confounded by load, node and cache differences, and old role logs were incomplete; no causal loading speedup is established. It ties on SLA at the listed lower loads.
